Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a protocol into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme protocol and deliver a live timeline: Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells for two T75 flasks split 1:6 into four
Resource limits: one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge, one microscope with haemocytometer, one operator.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells

Two T75 flasks at about 90 % confluence are split 1:6 into four new flasks. The room has one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge and one microscope with a haemocytometer. Only one flask can be open in the cabinet at a time, so the two flasks queue for it while the centrifuge and the microscope stay free. Work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells. One operator.

Preparation
1. Wipe down the cabinet, lay out pipettes and tubes, and let the blower run; 10 minutes.
2. Check both flasks on the microscope for confluence and contamination; 10 minutes.

Flask A
3. Aspirate the spent medium and rinse the monolayer with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes in the cabinet.
4. Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask and return it to the incubator for 5 minutes.
5. Knock the flask, check detachment and neutralise with 8 mL of medium; 5 minutes in the cabinet.
6. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube and spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
7. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
8. Count the cells on the haemocytometer; 6 minutes.
9. Seed two new T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes in the cabinet.
10. Return the new flasks to the incubator and leave them to settle overnight, at least 16 hours.

Flask B
11. Start flask B the moment flask A leaves the cabinet: aspirate and rinse with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes.
12. Trypsinise flask B in the incubator for 5 minutes.
13. Neutralise flask B as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again; 5 minutes.
14. Spin flask B at 300 × g for 5 minutes once the centrifuge is free.
15. Resuspend the flask B pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
16. Count flask B on the haemocytometer once flask A has been counted; 6 minutes.
17. Seed two more T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes.
18. Return them to the incubator to settle overnight alongside the first pair.

Finishing
19. Wipe the cabinet down, discard the waste and switch the blower to standby; 10 minutes.
20. Write the passage number, the split ratio and the counts into the culture log; 5 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. **Read-back.** This run passages two adherent HEK293 T75 flasks sitting at roughly 90 % confluence, splitting them 1:6 into four fresh T75 flasks — the text has each parent flask (A, then B) seeding two new flasks — so the output is four new T75 flasks that are then left to settle overnight. There is no clock time and no finishing time anywhere in the text, only the instruction that the hands-on work finishes as early as it can; the one fixed horizon is biological rather than diarised, the post-seeding overnight settle of at least 16 hours, which is the true tail of the protocol and the thing that ends the run. Everything is done by a single operator, so the person is a capacity-1 resource in their own right and the two flasks can never be worked in parallel — they interleave. Five instruments exist exactly once: one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge, one microscope with haemocytometer; the cabinet is the binding one because only one flask may be open in it at a time, which is why flask B starts the instant flask A leaves the cabinet (step 11) and is neutralised as soon as A is out again (step 13), while the centrifuge and microscope are explicitly free by the time each flask needs them — A spins before B needs it, A is counted before B is counted. The incubator does double duty: it gives each flask its 5-minute trypsin-EDTA incubation and later receives all four new flasks for the overnight settle. Nothing cold may touch the cells — medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA are pre-warmed throughout — so the water bath is a genuine prerequisite step for the reagents, not decoration. The text looks complete: all four sections (Preparation, Flask A, Flask B, Finishing) and steps 1–20 are present, nothing points at a section that is missing. One thing I've taken as written rather than reconciled: a 1:6 split would normally give six daughters per parent, yet the steps describe seeding two new flasks per parent, so I've treated 1:6 as the stated dilution ratio and the four-flask yield as the stated scale.
